author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The method parameter `page` is immediately overwritten by `page = Math.max(page, 1)`. After line 98 the name `page` carries a different semantic value than what was passed in, but the signature and every downstream use share the same name. A reader skimming the method body sees `page` used in `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName(page, ...)` and `addPaginationModel(page, ...)` without an obvious cue that it was clamped. Parameter reassignment defeats the compiler's ability to flag accidental use of the raw value after clamping.
findings.fix: Introduce a local variable: `int effectivePage = Math.max(page, 1);` and replace every subsequent use of `page` in the method body with `effectivePage`. The raw parameter `page` then goes unused after the clamp line, which makes the intent unambiguous.

findings.description: The new test declares `Page<Owner> tasks` to hold a page of owners. The name `tasks` is semantically wrong: it names work items, not owners. The naming checklist requires variables to be descriptive and proportional in scope. The pre-existing tests in the same file repeat the same mistake, but this diff reproduces it and is therefore in scope.
findings.fix: Rename the local variable to `ownerPage` (or `ownersPage`) in the new test method `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage`. The pre-existing uses in other methods are outside this diff's scope but should be cleaned up in a follow-on pass.

approved_aspects: Fix logic is correct: Math.max(page, 1) clamps all sub-1 values including negative integers
Comment on line 97 explains the intent adequately
Test method name `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage` is descriptive and follows BDD naming conventions
Test asserts `model().attribute("currentPage", 1)` which directly verifies the clamped value reaches the view model
Test structure follows four-phase arrangement with blank-line separation

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test method name processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage is an implementation name (names the method under call), not a behavior name. The testing brief (Test Naming, effective 2026-07-31) mandates the BDD school: the{Subject}Should{Outcome}. This test is new and post-cutoff so the school applies.

The fix is Math.max(page, 1), which clamps any value below 1 including -1, -100, and Integer.MIN_VALUE. Only page=0 is exercised. Values like -1 and a large negative are a distinct input class and are untested. A @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource entries for 0, -1, and -100 would cover the full clamping surface without duplicating test structure.
findings.fix: Replace the single @Test with a @ParameterizedTest / @CsvSource covering page values {0, -1, -100}; all three should assert HTTP 200, currentPage==1, and view owners/ownersList.

findings.description: new Owner() is called directly in a new test written after 2026-07-31. The testing brief (Test Data Construction) requires all object construction in post-cutoff tests to go through a factory method, not raw constructors. An anonymous createAnOwner() factory is the right pattern.
findings.fix: Introduce a package-scoped createAnOwner() factory method in the test class and replace new Owner() with createAnOwner().
